description: Insecurity Insight collects and analyses data on violence against civilians and on damage and destruction of vital civilian infrastructure in armed conflict, and publishes 43 datasets on the Humanitarian Data Exchange (count on 2026-09-26). The global Attacks on Health Care dataset holds incident and overview workbooks for 2016 to 2026 drawn from its monthly news brief, plus a file on looting of health supplies in the Sahel; a companion dataset covers attacks on public-health programmes such as vaccination, COVID-19 and Ebola responses. Country datasets, for example Ukraine, add incident workbooks on aid workers killed, injured, kidnapped or arrested, education in danger, explosive weapons, conflict incidents affecting food and water systems, and the data cited in the Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition's annual reports. Coverage: conflict-affected countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the DRC, India, Mali, Myanmar, Niger, Pakistan, Palestine, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Ukraine and Yemen. Access: Excel workbooks on HDX. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike; free. Caveats: records are collected from open sources, public reports and partner submissions; the organisation says they are neither complete nor representative and have not been independently verified. Simulation uses are event data on attacks against hospitals, schools and water and food facilities for conflict-damage scenarios, service-disruption studies and protection planning. Related records: the EWIPA explosive weapons and health facilities data and the Syria hospitals status data (services piece).
